findings.claim: Mathematics is a first-class formal-domain candidate, but its internal topology already contains domains, bridges and axes; root admission still requires explicit criteria.
Probability and Statistics are distinct identities; Statistics additionally functions as a cross-domain inferential/methodological axis.
Dynamical Systems, Systems Theory/Control and Systems Engineering are three distinct identities with specific bridge relations.
Geochemistry is a stable Earth↔chemistry bridge spanning planetary, atmospheric, hydrologic and biospheric contexts.
Physical Geography is a stable geography↔Earth/environment bridge and should not be collapsed into either generic Earth Science or human geography.
Genetics and Genomics are distinct but coupled identities; Genomics adds genome-scale technology, data and computation dimensions.

Information Science and Librarianship are overlapping but distinct: one centers inquiry into information organization/flow/use, the other includes professional/institutional information-access practice and infrastructure.

next: Repeat Whole-Foundational Topology Audit using Round2C; evaluate whether any Round1 unresolved candidates remain and whether topology grammar is now closed enough for a canonical-major-region admission experiment.

normalizedSpaces.label: Mathematics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: MSC2020 is a broad researcher-maintained taxonomy of the mathematical sciences. Mathematics warrants first-class formal-domain identity, while its many sections and cross-references argue against reducing all formal sciences to a single simple hierarchy.

normalizedSpaces.label: Probability theory and stochastic processes
normalizedSpaces.rationale: MSC2020 60-XX is a distinct major class with cross-references across mathematics, physics, biology, engineering, systems and information. It is related to but not identical with Statistics.

normalizedSpaces.label: Statistics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: MSC2020 62-XX is a distinct major class with foundational topics, decision theory, inference, experiment design and applications across sciences. Statistics is therefore both a formal domain and a cross-domain inferential axis, not synonymous with Probability.

normalizedSpaces.label: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
normalizedSpaces.rationale: MSC2020 37-XX is distinct and explicitly maps applications to mechanics, fluids, oceanography, meteorology, physics, biology and control. Dynamical systems is a cross-domain process/structure axis, not the same identity as systems theory or systems engineering.

normalizedSpaces.label: Systems theory and control
normalizedSpaces.rationale: MSC2020 93-XX explicitly identifies systems theory and control, including system structure, stability and stochastic systems. This mathematical/control identity is distinct from lifecycle-oriented Systems Engineering.

normalizedSpaces.label: Geochemistry
normalizedSpaces.rationale: The Geochemical Society frames geochemistry as applying chemistry to understanding Earth and the solar system, spanning solid Earth, atmospheres, hydrospheres, biospheres and extraterrestrial bodies. It is a stable Earth↔chemistry bridge.

normalizedSpaces.label: Physical geography
normalizedSpaces.rationale: AAG describes physical geography through geomorphology, climatology, biogeography, hydrology and soil science while emphasizing geography’s porous human/physical boundaries. Physical geography is neither generic Earth science nor merely human geography.

normalizedSpaces.label: Genetics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NHGRI distinguishes genetics as the study of genes and their roles in inheritance. Genetics therefore has a stable inheritance/process identity within biology and should not be collapsed into Genomics.

normalizedSpaces.label: Genomics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NHGRI distinguishes genomics as study of whole genomes and supports foundational genomic resources, technologies, experiments, data science and analytical tools. Genomics is a genetics-related but distinct biology↔computation↔medicine bridge.

normalizedSpaces.label: Information science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ASIS&T defines information science around properties/flows and the origination, organization, storage, retrieval, interpretation, transmission and use of recorded information, explicitly drawing on computing, cognition, mathematics, logic, linguistics, systems and library science. It warrants first-class identity.

normalizedSpaces.label: Librarianship and library studies
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ALA treats librarianship as a professional field prepared through library and information studies programs, with competencies specific to library/information environments. It overlaps information science but is not identical to the scientific inquiry domain.

policies.noConflation: Related fields remain distinct when source semantics support separate disciplinary identities.
policies.splitRepair: A census candidate may split into multiple normalized identities without preserving the old label as a canonical node.

repairs.reason: MSC2020 has separate major classes 60-XX and 62-XX; relation is overlap/cross-reference, not identity.
MSC2020 separates 37-XX Dynamical systems and 93-XX Systems theory; control. Systems Engineering remains a third distinct identity.
NHGRI distinguishes genetics (genes/inheritance) from genomics (whole genomes and genome-scale inquiry).
ASIS&T supports a scientific/inquiry identity for Information Science while ALA supports a professional Library and Information Studies/Librarianship identity; overlap does not imply equivalence.

scope: Seven unresolved Round1 candidates, with identity splits where evidence rejects the original combined label.
